Please note that LV2 and LV3 options’
performance and stability may varies due to CPU/DRAM’s condition.

An adequate cooling solution is recommended.

4:10752/10.help: Set CPU D2D Ratio from Range 15 to 40. 0 indicates no setting.

4:10752/11.help: Request Core Minimum Ratio. Limit Core minimum ratio for extreme overclocking and the ratio is in units of 100Mhz. The request value will be updated to minimum allowed one if it's too small. The request value will be updated to the maximum allowed one if it's too big. 0 indicates no setting.

4:10752/12.help: IA AC Loadline defined in 1/100 mOhms. A value of 100 = 1.00 mOhm, and 1255 = 12.55 mOhm. Range is 0-6249 (0-62.49 mOhms). 0 = AUTO/HW default. Uses BIOS mailbox command 0x2.

4:10752/13.help: IA DC Loadline defined in 1/100 mOhms. A value of 100 = 1.00 mOhm, and 1255 = 12.55 mOhm. Range is 0-6249 (0-62.49 mOhms). 0 = AUTO/HW default. Uses BIOS mailbox command 0x2.

4:10752/18.help:
Adjusts the CPU TjMAX temperature.
Notice: Higher temperature settings can potentially damage the CPU.

4:10752/19.help: Offset from factory set Tcc activation temprature at which the Thermal Control Circuit must be activated. Tcc will be activated at: Tcc Activation Temp - Tcc Activation Offset. Tcc Activation Offset range is 0 to 63.

4:10752/20.help: Tcc Offset Time Window for Running Average Temperature Limit(RATL) feature. The Tcc offset time window can range from 5ms to 448s.

4:10752/21.help: Adjusts the CPU Ring frequency. It affects all the non-core related parts of the CPU.

4:10752/22.help: Adjusts the CPU Ring frequency. It affects all the non-core related parts of the CPU.

4:10752/24.help: Enable = Turbo Boost operates at stock settings. Auto = Turbo Boost operates at stock settings, except when the BCLK frequency is altered. This can improve performance in single-threaded applications.

4:10752/27.help: Manually set 1-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be higher or equal to the 2-Core turbo ratio limit.

4:10752/28.help: Manually set 2-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be higher or equal to the 3-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/29.help: Manually set 3-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be higher or equal to the 4-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core and 2-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/30.help: Manually set 4-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 3-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/31.help: Manually set 5-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 4-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core/ 4-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/32.help: Manually set 6-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 5-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core/ 4-Core/ 5-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/33.help: Manually set 7-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 6-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core / 4-Core/ 5-Core/ 6-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/34.help: Manually set 8-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 7-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core / 4-Core/ 5-Core/ 6-Core/ 7-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/35.help: Manually set 9-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 8-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core / 4-Core/ 5-Core/ 6-Core/ 7-Core/ 8-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/36.help: Manually set 10-Core turbo ratio limit.Value will be lower than or equal to the 9-Core turbo ratio limit. 1-Core/ 2-Core/ 3-Core / 4-Core/ 5-Core/ 6-Core/ 7-Core/ 8-Core/ 9-Core limit must not be set to Auto.

4:10752/62.help: Allows you to set a current limit for CPU Turbo mode. When the CPU current exceeds the specified current limit, the CPU will automatically reduce the core frequency in order to reduce the current.

4:10752/64.help: This value must be between Max Efficiency Ratio (LFM) and Maximum non-turbo ratio set by Hardware (HFM).

4:10752/116.help: Set the number of CPU cores that are enabled.

4:10752/117.help: Set the number of CPU ATOM cores that are enabled.

4:10752/150.help: Enable/Disable Intel(R) Speed Shift Technology support. Enabling will expose the CPPC v2 interface to allow for hardware controlled P-states.

4:10752/152.help:
When enabled, the CPU core frequency and voltage will be reduced during system halt state to decrease power consumption.
Auto = BIOS to automatically configure this setting

4:10752/153.help: Processor will enter C3 state to lower power consumption when CPU is in idle state if enabled

4:10752/154.help: Processor will enter C6/C7 state to lower power consumption when CPU is in idle state if enabled

4:10752/155.help: Processor will enter C8 state to lower power consumption when CPU is in idle state if enabled

4:10752/156.help: Processor will enter C10 state to lower power consumption when CPU is in idle state if enabled

4:10752/157.help: Select a CPU C-State mode for power-saving when the system is idle.

4:10752/158.help:
When enabled, the CPU core frequency and voltage will be reduced when the CPU is overheated.
Auto = BIOS automatically configure this setting.

4:10752/159.help: Enable or disable the power management feature that reduces the Ring Ratio by 3 ratios compared to the CPU Core Ratio.

4:10752/160.help: Disable = Disables the voltage reduction by the Thermal Velocity Boost when the processor is cold. Enable = Core voltage will be lowered based on the Core temperature when the Velocity Frequency Boost is enabled on the processor.

4:10752/161.help:
OCMB0x18[2] disable – Frequency clipping caused by the Thermal Velocity Boost feature.
enable – Frequency will be clipped when the processor is hot.

4:10752/166.help:
Select FLL Mode 
Disable = no overclocking 
Nominal = ratio overclocking (0.5-1x) reference clock frequency 
Elevated = BCLK overclocking (1-3x) reference clock frequency 
Extreme = BCLK overclocking (3-5x) reference clock frequency and ratio limited to 63

4:10752/167.help: Enable / Disable Core Ratio Above 85 Extension Mode. Enable - Max Overclocking Ratio Limit as specified by OCMB 0x1 command is 120; Disable - Max Overclocking Ratio Limit as specified by OCMB 0x1 command is 85.

4:10752/169.help: Voltage Regulator Fast Vmode ICC Limit. A value of 400 = 100A. A value of 0 corresponds to feature disabled (no reactive protection). This value represents the current threshold where the VR would initiate reactive protection if Fast Vmode is enabled. The value is represented in 1/4 A increments. Uses BIOS VR mailbox command 0x25.

4:10752/171.help: Voltage Regulator Fast Vmode ICC Limit. A value of 400 = 100A. A value of 0 corresponds to feature disabled (no reactive protection). This value represents the current threshold where the VR would initiate reactive protection if Fast Vmode is enabled. The value is represented in 1/4 A increments. Uses BIOS VR mailbox command 0x25.

4:10752/173.help: Voltage Regulator Fast Vmode ICC Limit. A value of 400 = 100A. A value of 0 corresponds to feature disabled (no reactive protection). 4:10752/177.help: Select VCCSA boot voltage between Nominal and High Voltage(up to 1.2/1.3V). VCCSA boot Voltage - the default voltage is Nominal, to support the high voltage, BIOS can program the EPOC2 bits to bump up voltage to up to 1.2/1.3V.  0 - Nominal. 1 - High Voltage(up to 1.2/1.3V).

4:10752/178.help: Select CPU Bandgap Reference Mode between Normal and Bandgap Bypassed. CPU Bandgap Reference Mode - the default voltage is Normal.

4:10869/1.help:
Internal AC/DC Loadline adjusts the CPU Vcore when the system is under loading. The options are to optimize the CPU Vcore automatically based on the CPU core.
Notice: Greater values may lead to higher Vcore and higher CPU/VRM temperatures.

4:10869/2.help:
Loadline calibration helps to prevent CPU voltage drop when the system is under loading. It also improves CPU overclocking stability.
Notice: Greater values may lead to higher Vcore and higher CPU/VRM temperatures.

4:10869/5.help: Increases the power threshold before over-current protection limits power. Greater values are preferred for higher-end overclocking scenarios. At “Auto”, BIOS automatically configures this setting.

4:10870/2.help:
Adjust the Internal CPU Vcore voltage. 
Auto = BIOS automatically configures this setting. 
Vcore voltages can be entered manually. 
Note: Extreme overclocked configurations may need higher Vcore voltage, which may incur higher temperatures.

4:10870/3.help: Selects between Legacy and Selection modes. Need Reset System after enabling OverClocking Feature to Initialize the default value. In Legacy Mode, setting a global offset for the entire VF curve. In Selection modes, setting a selected VF point.

4:10870/4.help:
Increase or decrease the upper or lower voltage limit for the Internal CPU Vcore. 
Note. This option is only available when CPU Vcore (above) is set to ‘Normal’.

4:10870/5.help: Specifies the Offset Voltage applied to the Selected VF Point 1. This voltage is specified in millivolts. Uses Mailbox MSR 0x150, cmd 0x11, Param1 0, Param2 0x1. Range -500 to 500 mV

4:10015/340.help:
Please input HEX value.

Bit0
 '0' No override [Default]
 '1' Only allow countries enabled in the following bits
Bit1 - USA
 '0' USA 6GHz disable
 '1' 6GHz allowed in USA
Bit2 - Rest of World
Bit3 - EU countries
Bit4 - South Korea
Bit5 - Brazil
Bit6 - Chile
Bit7 - Japan
Bit8 - Canada
Bit9 - Morocco
Bit10 - Mongolia
Bit11 - Malaysia
Bit31:12 - Reserved

4:10015/343.help:
Control Enablement UNII-4 over certificate modules
Please input HEX value.

FCC
Bit0 - Apply changes over FCC, UNII-4 setting within module certification (Default Intel module definitions)
 '0' Work with WiFi FW/OTP definitions
 '1' Apply changes
Bit1 - UNII-4 mode on FCC
 '0' Disable UNII-4
 '1' Enable UNII-4

ETSI
Bit2 - Apply changes over ETSI, UNII-4 setting within module certification (Default Intel module definitions)
Bit3 - UNII-4 mode on ETSI

Bit31:4 - Reserved shall set to zeros

4:10015/344.help:

Please input HEX value.

Bit0 - EU
Bit1 - Japan
Bit2 - China, applied only in case of China BIOS or DRS in China Enabled
Bit3 - USA
Bit31:4 - Reserved shall set to zeros

Bit0 - Enable TAS feature.

 '1' Enabled TAS IEC optimization regulatory averaging time
Bit31:3 - Reserved

4:10072/8.prompt: Per Core P State OS control mode
4:10072/8.help: Enable/Disable Per Core P state OS control mode. When set, the highest core request is used for all other core requests.

4:10072/9.prompt: HwP Autonomous Per Core P State
4:10072/9.help: Disable Autonomous PCPS Autonomous will request the same value for all cores all the time.

4:10072/10.help: Enable EPP grouping Autonomous will request the same values for all cores with same EPP. Disable EPP grouping autonomous will not necessarily request same values for all cores with same EPP.

4:10072/11.help: Enable/Disable HWP Lock support in Misc Power Management MSR.

4:10072/16.help: Enable/Disable Platform Power Limit 1 programming. If this option is enabled, it activates the PL1 value to be used by the processor to limit the average power of given time window.

4:10072/17.help: Platform Power Limit 1 Power in Milli Watts/Percent. BIOS will round to the nearest 1/8W when programming. Any value can be programmed between Max and Min Power Limits (specified by PACKAGE_POWER_SKU_MSR). For example, if 12.50W, enter 12500, if 12%, enter 12000, if 50%, enter 50000. This setting will act as the new PL1 value for the Package RAPL algorithm.

4:10072/18.help: Platform Power Limit 1 Time Window value in seconds. The value may vary from 0 to 128. 0 = default values. Indicates the time window over which Platform Processor Base Power (TDP) value should be maintained.

4:10072/19.help: Enable/Disable Platform Power Limit 2 programming. If this option is disabled, BIOS will program the default values for Platform Power Limit 2.

4:10072/20.help: Platform Power Limit 2 Power in Milli Watts/Percent. BIOS will round to the nearest 1/8W when programming. Any value can be programmed between Max and Min Power Limits (specified by PACKAGE_POWER_SKU_MSR). For example, if 12.50W, enter 12500, if 12%, enter 12000, if 50%, enter 50000. This setting will act as the new Max Turbo Power (PL2) value for the Package RAPL algorithm.

4:10072/21.help: Enable/Disable Power Limit 4 override. If this option is disabled, BIOS will leave the default values for Power Limit 4.

4:10072/22.help: Power Limit 4 in Milli Watts. BIOS will round to the nearest 1/8W when programming. For 12.50W, enter 12500. If the value is 0, BIOS leaves default value

4:10072/23.help: Power Limit 4 Lock. When enabled PL4 configurations are locked during OS. When disabled PL4 configuration can be changed during OS.

4:10072/25.help: Configure Power Limit 4 Boost in Watts. The value 0 means disable.

4:10072/26.help: Enable/Disable C1E. When enabled, CPU will switch to minimum speed when all cores enter C-State.

4:10072/27.help: Enable/Disable CPU Power Management. Allows CPU to go to C states when it's not 100% utilized.

4:10072/32.help: Disable - to 1 to disable the Cstate Pre-Wake

4:10072/33.help: When set, will map IO_read instructions sent to IO registers PMG_IO_BASE_ADDRBASE+offset to MWAIT(offset)

4:10072/34.help: Maximum Package C State Limit Setting. Cpu Default: Leaves to Factory default value.Auto: Initializes to deepest available Package C State Limit.

4:10072/50.help: This option is to disable SoC's aggressive throttling to manage floor power (minimum power consumption). Disabling this might effectively raise power floor of the SoC and may lead to stability issues.

4:10072/51.help: When this option is enabled, SoC can disconnect secondary/external display to lower SoC floor power. When disabled, display disconnect will not be used by SoC.

4:10072/52.help: When this option is enabled, SoC can reduce PCIe Gen speed to lower SoC floor power. When disabled, Pcie Gen speed reduction option will not be used by SoC.

4:10072/55.help: Enable Dual Tau Boost feature. This is only applicable for Desktop 35W/65W/125W sku. When DPTF is enabled this feature is ignored.

4:10299/4.help: Defines the per-core HT disable mask where: 1 - Disable selected logical core HT, 0 - is ignored. Input is in HEX and each bit maps to a logical core. Ex. A value of '1F' would disable HT for cores 4,3,2,1 and 0. Default is 0, all cores have HT enabled. Range is 0 - 0x7F for max 8 cores. You can only disable up to MAX_CORE_COUNT - 1.

Range is 40 MHz - 1000 MHz w/ 10KHz.

4:10299/19.help: Select PVD Mode Value from Range 1 to 3. 0x0 = div-1 (VCO = Output clock), 0x1 = div-2 (VCO = 2x Output clock), 0x2 = div-4 (VCO = 4x Output clock), 0x3 = div-8 (VCO = 8x Output clock)

4:10299/22.help: Select FLL Mode Value from Range 1 to 3. 0x0 = no overclocking, 0x1 = ratio overclocking with nominal (0.5-1x) reference clock frequency, 0x2 = BCLK overclocking with elevated (1-3x) reference clock frequency, 0x3 = BCLK overclocking with extreme elevated (3-5x) reference clock frequency and ratio limited to 63

4:10299/23.help: Set CPU D2D Ratio from Range 15 to 40. 0 indicates no setting.

4:10299/24.help: Request Core Minimum Ratio. Limit Core minimum ratio for extreme overclocking and the ratio is in units of 100Mhz. The request value will be updated to minimum allowed one if it's too small. The request value will be updated to the maximum allowed one if it's too big. 0 indicates no setting.

hardware_profile._doc: Runtime state the real BIOS fills in at boot (not stored in the image). Values are keyed by varstore name -> byte offset. 'varstore_defaults' applies one value to every question in a varstore; 'values' overrides single offsets. Calibrated against the overview video (Core Ultra 9 285K, 2x24GB Kingston DDR5 XMP 8200, admin access).

system.memory: 2x24GB Kingston DDR5 (XMP 8200 MT/s), slots DDR5_A2 + DDR5_B2

hardware_profile._values_doc: ProcMitAttrib+0/+1 = P/E-core count. MemMitAttrib +1 = kit has a profile, +9 = XMP+EXPO kit, +10 = EXPO kit, +11 = XMP kit, +3..+7 = XMP profile 1..5 absent (decoded from the firmware's own conditions). The emulator overrides these from the selected parts.
